screens.name: Home — available omen, 390/430, Chrome/WebKit
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–35 show the orb-led home at both text scales and widths, with reported browser contrast and layout checks.
findings: Increase the normal-size example question’s prominence so it reads as useful inspiration above the dominant orb.

screens.name: Home — omen loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 58 shows Finding your omen beneath the available primary interaction.
findings: Demonstrate the omen loading status announcement and its transition to success or unavailability.

screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and expanded daily limit
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–36 show no saved omen, tomorrow’s next attempt and an expanded explanation of the consumed attempt.
findings: Expose the consumed-attempt explanation beside the unavailable status so users need not expand Daily limit to understand it.

screens.name: Home — constrained-height large text
screens.evidence: Sheets 56 and 61 show the large-text omen section continuing below the visible area above the tab bar.
findings: Reduce decorative hero space at short heights to bring more omen content into the initial viewport.

screens.name: Question entry — type or speak
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4, 36 and 58 show a consistent orb, title and primary typing action across settled and transition captures.
findings: Demonstrate keyboard focus and activation for the secondary speaking action.

screens.name: Question composer — myself and named person
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–6, 16, 56 and 58 show labeled questions, subject switching and submission, supported by draft and explicit-send checks.
findings: Shorten the repeated explanatory paragraph to keep the question visually dominant at 200% text.

screens.name: Question composer — constrained height and long question
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show scrolling question fields with submission retained in the simulated 500px viewport.
findings: Make the availability of content above the focused field more apparent when the subject and disclosure have scrolled away.

screens.name: Named-person selection — selected and editing
screens.evidence: Sheet 5 shows Someone selected, a labeled Alex field, privacy explanation and explicit confirmation.
findings: Keep Cancel changes readily discoverable at 200% text alongside the confirmation action.

screens.name: Voice entry — start failure
screens.evidence: Sheets 38 and 58 show a microphone-start failure with typing and retry recovery, while speech boundaries are explicitly mocked.
findings: Demonstrate distinct permission-denied and unavailable-browser recovery states before treating voice recovery as complete.

screens.name: Adaptive cards — unanswered first, middle and final steps
screens.evidence: Sheets 7–9, 55 and 61 show compact questions, progress, unselected radios and disabled Continue or Reveal.
findings: Retain the explicit instruction and disabled-action relationship for variable-length generated questions.

screens.name: Adaptive cards — selected, keyboard focus and restored answers
screens.evidence: Sheets 3, 10, 24–26 and 62 show selected and focused choices, supported by keyboard, restoration and single-advance checks.
findings: Preserve the separate selected and focus indicators when extending the answer controls.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 9 shows the complete question, Your answer label, Back to choices and an explanation for disabled submission.
findings: Clarify the distinction between the top back arrow and Back to choices if they lead to different destinations.

screens.name: Custom answer — populated and constrained long answer
screens.evidence: Sheets 36–37 show populated scrolling answers with the question and Reveal retained at constrained height.
findings: Verify that field scrolling and page scrolling remain distinguishable with browser keyboard navigation at 200% text.

screens.name: AI consent — review action before permission
screens.evidence: Sheet 19 shows Review AI consent replacing submission, with reported zero requests before a separate Ask action.
findings: Retain the explicit permission-review action and draft preservation across both consent decisions.

screens.name: AI consent — disclosure and grant/decline
screens.evidence: Sheets 18–19 show provider, input categories, purpose and grant/decline within the scrollable consent flow.
findings: Replace the terse Permission only sentence with a direct statement that allowing access does not submit the question.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheet 39 shows explicit age choices and explains that skipped birthdays use limits for ages 13–17.
findings: Explain the practical meaning of age-appropriate limits without requiring users to interpret policy terminology.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40 show optionality, adjacent Skip and date fields reflowing into two rows at 200%.
findings: Retain the nearby Skip action and full date labels through validation and text enlargement.

screens.name: Age restriction — onboarding and birthday editor
screens.evidence: Sheets 1 and 40–41 show a clear restriction and birthday correction path, supported by under-13 rejection checks.
findings: Use a consistent accessible focus treatment for the restriction heading across entry paths.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheet 41 shows actual-birthday guidance, labeled fields and Check birthday, with the return action below the large-text viewport.
findings: Reduce introductory spacing so the return path is easier to discover at 200% text.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected, skipped and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 42–43 show optional choices, a selected checkmark and the primary action changing from Skip focus to Meet the Ball.
findings: Capitalize Gemini consistently with the birth-profile presentation.

screens.name: Birthday editor — populated
screens.evidence: Sheet 79 shows populated fields, Save, Cancel and removal disclosure, supported by save/reload and cancellation checks.
findings: Preserve the clear separation between saving, cancelling and removing birthday data.

screens.name: Birthday editor — invalid and incomplete drafts
screens.evidence: Sheets 1–2 show retained invalid and incomplete drafts with specific messages but visually unchanged field borders.
findings: Associate each validation message with the affected fields and add a visible invalid-field cue beyond the general message.

screens.name: Birth details — time entry and forgotten confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 6 and 78–79 show optional time entry, 24-hour guidance and confirmation that time/place were forgotten while birthday remains.
findings: Add a direct I don’t know my birth time action instead of instructing users to return to You.

screens.name: Birth details — city entry
screens.evidence: Sheets 77–78 show an empty labeled city field, disabled search and a clear statement of what is sent.
findings: Supply visible search-loading, no-results and failure examples to complete assessment of city recovery.

screens.name: Birth profile — calculated Moon and rising
screens.evidence: Sheet 55 shows a calculated result, local-storage statement, location/time and edit/forget actions.
findings: Show this completed profile at 200% text to establish the same readable hierarchy as its entry forms.

screens.name: Planning and research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 53–54, 59 and 62–63 distinguish checking the question from forming the forecast and retain cancellation and credit reassurance.
findings: Keep the stage-specific explanation visually prominent when the decorative orb is removed at large text.

screens.name: Recovery — prolonged wait and timeout
screens.evidence: Sheet 62 shows a changed long-wait message and explicit timeout recovery, supported by a reported real 60-second timeout test.
findings: Demonstrate announcement of the long-wait and timeout changes without requiring users to refocus the page.

screens.name: Recovery — planning and prediction errors
screens.evidence: Sheets 20–21 and 60 show retry, question editing and prediction-stage answer review, with retained answers reported.
findings: Carry the explicit no-reading-spent reassurance into the real connection-error variant.

screens.name: Sensitive question — support referral and general redirection
screens.evidence: Sheets 57, 60 and 66–67 show both direct support referral and a general redirection with no-credit/no-memory reassurance.
findings: Put the humane explanation before the support button so its purpose is understood before activation.

screens.name: Forecast opening — normal and golden
screens.evidence: Sheets 43–47 show intact-orb charge, fracture and forecast settling, supported by reported timing, frame-rate and interruption checks.
findings: Keep forecast text sharper and more stable during the settle phase visible in the intermediate captures.

screens.name: Forecast opening — reduced motion, skip and interrupted paths
screens.evidence: Sheets 43, 45 and 48 show settled reduced, skipped and interrupted paths, supported by single-save and no-replay checks.
findings: Retain equivalent final content and direct access when the opening animation is bypassed.

screens.name: Forecast — settled and expanded actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 63–66 show prominent forecast text, qualification, reminder and progressively disclosed actions at both scales.
findings: Make the reminder’s relationship to the forecast horizon explicit when its date precedes the predicted outcome.

screens.name: Check-in — initial and unsaved selection
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–13 and 49 show original questions and outcome radios, with reported nonmutating drafts and all initial choices visible.
findings: Replace Choose again in the initial state with Select an outcome, then save.

screens.name: Check-in — saved yes, no and waiting
screens.evidence: Sheets 12 and 50–51 show distinct saved outcomes and disabled unchanged submission, supported by persistence and correction checks.
findings: Retain the explicit Saved label so disabled submission is not mistaken for a failed save.

screens.name: Check-in — forecast and additional actions expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11, 48–49 and 54–55 show disclosures below the outcome controls and credit-dependent additional actions.
findings: Add spacing around focused disclosure rows so their focus outline does not crowd the preceding helper text.

screens.name: Evidence — overview
screens.evidence: Sheets 17 and 64 show four clearly separated evidence destinations with explanatory subtitles and return navigation.
findings: Use a more explicit overview title alongside Behind the mist so the destination is immediately recognizable.

screens.name: Evidence — answers, long fixtures and real recorded context
screens.evidence: Sheets 15, 21–22 and 56 show separated answers, original question labels where available and an unexplained Answer 3 in the real-flow view.
findings: Label the real-flow Answer 3 value as its actual context type when known, or explicitly mark its original label as unavailable.

screens.name: Evidence — assumptions
screens.evidence: Sheets 16, 22 and 55 include long fixture assumptions and a real-flow Assumptions screen containing only a generic speculative disclaimer.
findings: State that no separate assumptions were recorded when the available content is only a disclaimer.

screens.name: Evidence — full reasoning and legacy passages
screens.evidence: Sheets 17, 23 and 65–66 show preserved legacy reasoning under neutral Passage labels rather than invented semantic headings.
findings: Identify legacy text as an unstructured explanation so Passage numbering does not imply meaningful analytical sections.

screens.name: Evidence — short Why and limits
screens.evidence: Sheets 57 and 59 separate recorded context, scenario assumption and limits in real-flow explanations.
findings: Provide a 200% capture of this structured real-flow explanation to verify its enlarged reading experience.

screens.name: Evidence — background sources
screens.evidence: Sheets 18 and 23–24 clearly distinguish background material from forecast verification and show dated source entries.
findings: Demonstrate external-link destination and failure handling without treating synthetic source fixtures as evidence quality.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 27–28 and 73–74 show a concise empty state, local-storage explanation and Ask the Ball action with stable transitions.
findings: Retain the direct first-reading action and concise local-storage explanation.

screens.name: History — populated, stress and persisted outcomes
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–27 and 61 show dated questions, forecasts, check-in links and persisted outcome markers.
findings: Reduce headline dominance at 200% text so a history entry’s date, status and opening action are easier to scan together.

screens.name: Sky — sample stars and selected question
screens.evidence: Sheets 57, 60 and 72–76 show selected themes, sample questions and an accessible large-text grid replacing the constellation layout.
findings: Bring the selected question closer to the theme controls at 200% text so the effect of selection is immediately visible.

screens.name: Circles — offline and retry failure
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–15 show explicit unavailability, retry and changed failure feedback while authenticated social behavior remains unconfigured.
findings: Shorten the secondary promotional section at large text so recovery remains the clear focus.

screens.name: Plans — yearly, monthly and exhausted allowance
screens.evidence: Sheets 52–53, 60 and 74–75 show selected billing periods, total prices, pack alternatives and explicit simulation labels.
findings: Keep the test-mode explanation and plan identity easily retrievable when enlarged options fill the viewport.

screens.name: You — populated and empty memory
screens.evidence: Sheets 56, 61 and 76–80 show profile facts, allowance, memory states and edit/forget actions.
findings: Reduce repeated vertical separators and spacing so profile, plan and memory sections remain easier to scan at 200%.

screens.name: You — display, sound and saved-data controls
screens.evidence: Sheet 68 shows labeled switches, large-text selection and links to privacy, plans and data removal.
findings: Demonstrate keyboard focus and announced state changes for each switch, including ambient sound.

screens.name: Share — preview and expanded invitation options
screens.evidence: Sheets 59 and 68–72 show a portrait preview, image-text alternative, download action and privacy explanation.
findings: Reduce preview height at 200% text to expose the download action sooner.

screens.name: Share — preparing, completed and failed export
screens.evidence: Sheets 57, 68 and 70 show preparing, download-started and retry states supported by held-encoding and actual-export checks.
findings: Retain Download started rather than implying that the browser has confirmed the file was saved.

screens.name: Share — enlarged image and direct image text
screens.evidence: Sheets 59, 69 and 71–73 show enlarged portrait cards and a separate readable text view containing forecast and qualification.
findings: Keep the image-text route prominent because text inside the fixed-format artwork remains small in preview.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home and opening captures show the illustrated orb as the main visual anchor, with reported animation and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Scale the hero down further in short viewports to protect task content.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Core tab screens show persistent labels, selected gold underlines and a raised Ask orb at both text scales.
findings: Verify that focused content near the bottom remains fully visible above the raised Ask orb and fixed bar.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Sheets show a protected graphic wordmark and balance labels that wrap into two lines at 200%.
findings: Give the balance’s plans affordance a clearer cue than an underline alone.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream primary actions have consistent geometry, wrapping labels and visible disabled/busy variants with reported target checks.
findings: Preserve content-driven height and explicit disabled-state explanations.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text actions recur beside gold informational labels, sometimes differentiated only by placement or a fine rule.
findings: Use a consistent non-color affordance to distinguish actionable gold text from informational gold text.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Selected radios, focus outlines and explicit submission are shown with reported Space, arrow, Home/End and roving-Tab behavior.
findings: Retain selection without automatic advancement across every adaptive-card variant.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Composer captures show persistent labels, readable entered text and distinct focus borders with reported draft preservation.
findings: Keep the persistent label and focus ring when text overflows the field.

components.name: Large-text scrolling input
components.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show shortened, internally scrolling fields retaining explicit submission in a 500px viewport.
findings: Demonstrate keyboard traversal between the internally scrolling field and the surrounding scrollable page.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheet 68 shows labeled on/off switches but no focused switch or switch-specific keyboard evidence.
findings: Show focus, keyboard activation and exposed checked state for every settings switch.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Home captures include successful, loading, unavailable and expanded daily-limit omen states.
findings: Explain the unavailable attempt directly in the status instead of relying on a separate disclosure.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sky captures use a selected checkmark and gold star, replacing the constellation with a text grid at 200%.
findings: Keep the selection result near the controls in the enlarged layout.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Circles captures expose unavailability and retry results without representing a working authenticated service.
findings: Prioritize recovery over the large secondary marketing heading.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Populated history captures separate date, original question, forecast, reminder/outcome and opening action.
findings: Keep row metadata and its opening action closer to oversized forecast text.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Yearly and monthly states show checkmarks, billing totals and selected rules with reported shared-radio keyboard checks.
findings: Maintain the total annual charge beside the monthly equivalent at every text scale.

components.name: Share preview card
components.evidence: Share captures show portrait artwork, enlargement and a full text alternative, with an actual 1080×1920 export reported.
findings: Increase the preview’s forecast and qualification prominence relative to the orb.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Error, timeout, offline and safety captures provide explicit recovery choices and state-specific reassurance.
findings: Demonstrate live announcement of newly appearing notices across the recovery paths.

components.name: Typography and spacing
components.evidence: Fraunces headings and Manrope body text remain coherent across sheets, with several large-text views dominated by headings or long explanatory copy.
findings: Tighten large-text vertical spacing around supporting copy while preserving the full text scale.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: Mist and bronze gradients provide consistent borderless surfaces, supported by reported contrast and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Keep the strongest mist texture away from dense reading sections.

components.name: Birthday input group
components.evidence: Birthday captures show labeled day/month/year inputs, responsive reflow and retained invalid drafts.
findings: Add field-specific visible invalid cues and verify error associations.

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Age confirmation and restriction captures are backed by reported rejection, correction and no-bypass checks.
findings: Explain the user-facing effect of teen-safe limits in plain language.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Focus captures show optionality, selected checkmarks and explicit completion without forcing a preference.
findings: Keep the selected indicator independent of color.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: You and birth-chart captures show saved facts, local calculation/storage statements and edit/forget actions.
findings: Verify the completed chart and its forget confirmation at 200% text.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Time and city forms show optional steps, format guidance and search disclosure but no pictured search results or errors.
findings: Provide direct unknown-time recovery and visible city-search result/error states.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Named-person captures show selected Someone, a persistent First name label and an explicit Use this person action.
findings: Demonstrate empty-name validation and cancellation with an existing question draft.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Forecast and evidence captures show disclosure chevrons, separate overview routes and visible focused expansion states.
findings: Ensure disclosure chevrons describe expansion consistently when similar-looking links instead navigate to another screen.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Preparing, download-started and retry statuses are pictured and supported by held-encoding, single-flight and real-export evidence.
findings: Preserve distinct busy, initiated-download and failed-export wording.

components.name: Outcome selector and save status
components.evidence: Outcome captures and runtime evidence distinguish unsaved choice, unchanged saved value and each persisted outcome.
findings: Use initial-state instructions until an outcome has actually been saved.

components.name: AI permission surface
components.evidence: Consent captures show categorized disclosure and grant/decline, with reported preserved draft/focus and no permission-triggered requests.
findings: Make the separation between granting permission and submitting the question explicit in one plain sentence.

components.name: Step progress and back navigation
components.evidence: Question cards show numeric progress and step marks, with restoration on Back reported.
findings: Distinguish previous-step navigation from returning to answer choices in custom-answer mode.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments; the supplied runtime account was considered but not independently rerun.
The browser threshold is not met: multiple screens and components have A or F below 9.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility, excluding genuinely inapplicable nulls.
Corresponding normal, enlarged and transition captures are grouped; sampled transitions support visual continuity but do not independently establish motion quality.
Content extending beyond a screenshot is not treated as unreachable where scrolling is reported; no hard-gate failure is established by this material.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native Dynamic Type, actual keyboard, haptics, microphone hardware and native sharing remain unverified.
The 500px captures simulate constrained height and do not demonstrate a native keyboard.
Authenticated Circles and real payments are not demonstrated; the pictured offline and explicitly simulated states are assessed on their own merits.
Synthetic long-form content and layout predictions do not establish model quality, source quality or predictive accuracy.
City search results/errors, focused settings-switch states and several completed birth-detail states lack full pictured coverage.
No previous-round comparison or independently observed before/after change is available; these scores do not certify improvement over prior rounds.
Reported automated contrast, target-size and axe results support browser assessment but do not replace representative assistive-technology use.
topFixes: Make the real Assumptions view explicitly acknowledge absent recorded assumptions instead of presenting a disclaimer as an assumption.
Replace unexplained real-flow evidence labels such as Answer 3 with known context labels or an explicit unavailable-label statement.
Correct initial check-in instructions from Choose again to Select an outcome, then save.
Reduce decorative space and supporting-copy height in constrained and 200% layouts, especially Home, History and Share.
Add visible field-specific birthday errors and demonstrate their accessible associations.
Clarify secondary-action affordances and distinguish disclosure expansion from navigation.
Expose the consumed omen-attempt explanation directly in its unavailable state.
Complete browser evidence for switch keyboard behavior, dynamic-status announcements, city-search recovery and empty named-person validation.
